subject: Performance SLOs — context window & token limits (follow-up)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@finco.com>, Bob Singh <b.singh@finco.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery — Performance SLOs & context window

Hi Alice / Bob —

Great to chat earlier today. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can size a PoC and recommend the right Dedicated pool / config. Attaching the call notes + an initial SLO draft for your review (20270428-finco-slo-draft.pdf).

Recap (high level)
- Primary use case: document summarization + real-time assistant for traders (ingest long docs, apply retrieval + summarization, sometimes multi-step)
- Expected traffic (initial): ~500 qps peak, steady-state 120 qps
- Typical request shape: input (prompt + retrieved context) ~2k tokens average, with spikes up to 20k tokens for large docs; response size average 300–600 tokens, up to 2k tokens for full summaries
- Streaming: important for the live assistant workflow (progressive output while model generates)
- Compliance: all inference in Private/Dedicated environment required for production

Clarifying questions for sizing and latency SLOs
1) Context window cap: you mentioned some workflows will need ~32k token context for long-doc summarization — can you confirm the % of requests that will hit >8k tokens vs >32k tokens?
2) Latency targets: for the live assistant, what p95 end-to-end latency target do you need for the user to consider the experience acceptable? (example: <=300ms for short prompts, <=1s for 4k contexts, 2–3s OK for 32k?)
3) Concurrency & burst tolerance: 500 qps peak — is that sustained for minutes or short spikes (seconds)? Do you expect many concurrent long-context streams (e.g., 50+ concurrent streams at once)?

Next steps
- Dylan & Michael to propose an initial architecture (model variant, batch/concurrency settings, streaming configuration) and a Dedicated sizing recommendation.
- We’ll run a short PoC: 2–4 weeks, focused on throughput/latency with your representative prompts.
- Marissa to send updated SLO doc and proposed commercial terms for Dedicated.

Thanks — appreciate the time today. If you can reply with the answers to Q1–Q3 above, Dylan will map that to concrete perf targets.

—
Marissa Cole

Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery — Performance SLOs & context window

Thanks Marissa — adding technical detail from the infra/SE side.

Short answers up front:
- We can support streaming for outputs of any size; streaming reduces perceived latency but has slightly higher tail variance for very long outputs.
- For context >8k tokens we recommend a different memory/quantization profile and larger GPU instances; expect p95 to increase relative to 4k baselines (roughly 2–4x depending on model and batching).

Notes / assumptions for PoC sizing:
- Baseline model: open-architecture LLM (32k variant) — we’ll propose two model configs: latency-optimized (~fp16/kv cache friendly) and throughput-optimized (int8/quantized). We'll include fallback routing.
- Token processing: for inputs ~2k tokens + outputs ~500 tokens, expect per-request token compute of ~2.5k tokens (we count prompt + generated).
- Throughput: 500 qps of short requests (2k-in/500-out) => sustained token rate ~1.25M tokens/sec; sustained 500 qps at 20k context is a different regime (much higher memory bandwidth and lower batching benefits).
- Concurrency: streaming use-case with ~50 concurrent streams implies we should size reserved concurrency and use continuous batching for non-streaming calls to maximize utilization.

Latency guidance (rough estimates for PoC; final numbers after benching)
- Short contexts (<=1k tokens total): p95 <= 200ms on latency-optimized config
- Medium contexts (~4k total): p95 ~ 300–600ms depending on prompt complexity and batching
- Large contexts (>=16k, up to 32k): p95 can range 1–3s; we can improve by allocating larger instances and tuning KV cache and kernel selection, but cost increases.

Streaming notes
- Streaming will give better perceived latency for the assistant UI but we’ll need to ensure we provision for open long-running connections. For many concurrent streams, we recommend a Dedicated pool that separates streaming workers from batch workers.

Action items for PoC
- Alice/Bob: provide representative sample prompts + distribution of context sizes (percentiles) so we can bench with realistic load.
- Redwood (Dylan/Michael): produce two config proposals (latency-optimized and cost-optimized) with expected p95 numbers and cost estimates.

Onward — happy to jump on a quick 30-min tech call tomorrow if useful.

—
Dylan Brooks
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dylan.brooks@redwood.com

From: Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@finco.com>

Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery — Performance SLOs & context window

Thanks Marissa / Dylan — good notes. Quick answers to your clarifying Qs:

Q1) Context window distribution (approx):
- ~70% of requests: <=4k tokens total (prompt + retrieved context)
- ~20%: 4k–16k tokens
- ~8%: 16k–32k tokens
- ~2%: >32k (very large doc ingestion, can be handled as separate batch jobs)

Q2) Latency targets (customer expectations):
- Live assistant (interactive): perceived p95 ideally <=500ms for <=4k contexts; <=1.5s is acceptable for 4k–16k; for 16k–32k we can accept up to ~3s p95 for initial rollouts but would like to improve over time.
- Non-interactive batch summarization: throughput prioritized over tail latency; nightly jobs can take minutes.

Q3) Concurrency & bursts:
- Peak 500 qps is a realistic target for high market hours; peaks typically last several minutes (5–20 minutes) rather than sustained hours.
- Concurrent streams: expect ~40–60 concurrent interactive users at peak (so assume 50 concurrent streams as a planning number).

Other notes:
- Streaming is required for the trader assistant UI — incremental tokens should be emitted as generated.
- We will provide a sample dataset of 200 representative prompts and their context-size distribution by EOD Friday (I’ll drop it in the shared Drive link).

Thanks — happy to sync if you want to walk the dataset with us.

Best,
Alice Morgan
Head of ML Products | FinCo
alice.morgan@finco.com

Subject: Re: Discovery — Performance SLOs & context window (next steps)

Thanks Alice — that distribution is really helpful. Summarizing agreement and next steps so we’re all aligned:

Agreed SLO targets for PoC (bench targets, to be validated after Redwood benching):
- Interactive (<=4k): p95 <= 500ms (latency-optimized config)
- Interactive (4k–16k): p95 <= 1.5s
- Interactive (16k–32k): p95 <= 3s (initial)
- Streaming: incremental token emission for all interactive flows; provisioned to support ~50 concurrent streams during peak
- Throughput: Dedicated trial to handle 500 qps peak for short requests; sustained baseline planning for 120 qps

PoC plan / next steps
1) FinCo to upload 200 sample prompts + distribution (Alice) — ETA: EOD Friday (Drive link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3cSLOsummary)
2) Redwood (Dylan/Michael): run bench tests against the provided dataset with two configs (latency-optimized and cost-optimized) — deliverable: bench report + recommended Dedicated sizing and expected cost estimate (5 business days after receiving samples)
3) Commercial: Marissa to share Dedicated pricing tier and proposed term sheet for a 3-month trial (attached: redwood-dedicated-pricing.pdf).
4) Technical deep-dive: schedule 30–60m call next week to review bench results and tune streaming/concurrency.

Attachments: SLO_summary_20270430.docx, redwood-dedicated-pricing.pdf

If that all looks right I’ll send a formal SOW + trial agreement and we can kick off the trial as soon as the sample prompts are uploaded.
